sources.citation: Brendan D. McKay, Isomorph-Free Exhaustive Generation, Journal of Algorithms 26 (1998), 306–324.
sources.exact_result_paraphrase: Theorem 1 proves that, under the canonical-construction-path axioms, scan(X0,n) outputs exactly one labelled representative of each unlabelled descendant isomorphism class up to the order bound. The procedure iterates over Aut(X)-orbits of admissible upper objects. In the graph specialization, an upper object <X,W> appends one new vertex joined to W.
c6_overlap: augmentation from a fixed base graph
missing_from_c6_target: no FCC/HCP native realizability constraint
no rooted weighted frontier observable [G,x]
no theorem that all realizable J_x over one compressed observable form one successor-equivalence orbit
sources.import_value: Use canonical construction path/orbit representatives as the enumeration skeleton for a future exact C7 native two-shell slot-assignment classifier.

sources.citation: Deisiane Lopes Gonçalves and Bhalchandra D. Thatte, A refinement of Kelly's lemma for graph reconstruction for counting rooted subgraphs, arXiv:2312.17022 (2023).
sources.exact_result_paraphrase: Kelly's lemma counts copies of a smaller graph from the vertex-deleted deck. The authors show that the desired refinement for rooted subgraphs with the root at the deleted vertex fails in general, while a multiset of rooted subgraphs of fixed height k can be counted when the graph radius exceeds k; an analogous edge-reconstruction statement is also proved.
c6_overlap: recoverability from a compressed collection of graph observations
missing_from_c6_target: input is a deletion deck, not one rooted weighted frontier graph
conclusion is subgraph counting, not exact successor reconstruction
no native FCC/HCP completion realizability
sources.import_value: Negative caution: rooted information is not automatically reconstructible from coarser graph data; it gives no implication for the specific G0->J_x map.

sources.citation: Gustav A. Hedlund, Endomorphisms and automorphisms of the shift dynamical system, Mathematical Systems Theory 3 (1969), 320–375.
sources.exact_result_paraphrase: The Curtis–Hedlund–Lyndon characterization identifies cellular automata with continuous shift-commuting maps; equivalently their global update is induced uniformly by a finite local rule on the full configuration.
missing_from_c6_target: uses the full local configuration rather than a lossy rooted weighted graph quotient
requires translation-equivariant global dynamics
does not reconstruct hidden completion data from a compressed observable
no FCC/HCP realizability orbit theorem
sources.import_value: Confirms that locality from full configuration is standard; C7 is instead an injectivity/equivalence question after information loss.

sources.citation: Gilles Bertrand and Grégoire Malandain, A new characterization of three-dimensional simple points, Pattern Recognition Letters 15 (1994), 169–175.
sources.exact_result_paraphrase: A three-dimensional simple point is characterized using only two connected-component counts computed in the point's neighborhood, avoiding explicit genus/hole calculations; the paper proves the validity of the local characterization.
c6_overlap: a bounded local neighborhood can decide a global-topology-preservation predicate
missing_from_c6_target: cubic digital grid rather than FCC/HCP
predicate is simple-point/topology preservation, not exact weighted-frontier successor
uses neighborhood occupancy data, not [G,x] alone
sources.import_value: Shows that local sufficiency for topological predicates is mature prior art and cannot by itself support a novelty claim.

sources.citation: Gilles Bertrand, Simple points, topological numbers and geodesic neighborhoods in cubic grids, Pattern Recognition Letters 15 (1994), 1003–1011.
sources.exact_result_paraphrase: For the {6,26} and {6,18} connectivity pairs in the 3D cubic grid, topological numbers defined from geodesic neighborhoods characterize simple points by two local conditions.
missing_from_c6_target: different grid/connectivity
only topology-preservation predicate
no weighted frontier successor or completion-orbit uniqueness
sources.import_value: Additional classic boundary for local digital-topology claims.

sources.citation: Gábor Karai, Péter Kardos and Kálmán Palágyi, Sufficient Conditions for Topology-Preserving Parallel Reductions on the Face-Centered Cubic Grid, Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision 66 (2024), 271–292.
sources.exact_result_paraphrase: For three types of binary pictures on the 3D FCC grid, the paper gives sufficient conditions for topology-preserving parallel reductions; some conditions verify a proposed reduction and others yield deletion rules. It also gives local characterizations of P-simple points whose simultaneous deletion preserves topology.
c6_overlap: one-step modification of a digital object
missing_from_c6_target: deletion/topology preservation rather than addition/frontier exposure
binary neighborhood information is richer than abstract rooted weighted G0
no HCP result
no J_x realization orbit or exact weighted-successor classification
sources.import_value: Prevents novelty inflation from merely having an FCC-local point-update criterion.

sources.citation: Lidija Čomić and Benedek Nagy, A topological 4-coordinate system for the face centered cubic grid, Pattern Recognition Letters 83 (2016), 67–74.
sources.exact_result_paraphrase: The proposed symmetric FCC 4-coordinate system is proved unambiguous and consistent, and incidence/boundary/co-boundary/adjacency relations among grid cells are expressible by simple integer operations on coordinates.
missing_from_c6_target: coordinates supply a richer native embedding than [G,x]
does not infer hidden slot identities from a compressed frontier graph
no HCP and no successor-equivalence orbit theorem
sources.import_value: Useful implementation carrier after a native slot assignment is chosen, but not an injectivity theorem for G0.

sources.citation: Tomoyasu Yokoyama, Kazuhide Ichikawa and Hisashi Naito, From polyhedra to crystals: a graph-theoretic framework for crystal structure generation, CrystEngComm 28 (2026), 2293–2304.
sources.exact_result_paraphrase: The framework encodes space-filling polyhedra by a dual periodic graph and obtains crystal structures by standard realization; it demonstrates reconstruction of FCC, HCP and BCC structures from those richer periodic-graph inputs.
missing_from_c6_target: global dual periodic graph is much richer than local rooted weighted frontier G0
standard realization is not hidden-completion recovery
no local one-step frontier successor or same-G0 J_x uniqueness theorem
sources.import_value: Documents a recent FCC/HCP graph-reconstruction direction but not the C6/C7 theorem family.

mature_prior_art_components: finite-local-rule determination from full cellular configurations
local digital-topology predicates, including FCC-specific topology-preserving reductions
FCC coordinate carriers that exactly encode native incidence
search_bounded_unmatched_core: injectivity or successor-equivalence of globally native-realizable J_x completions over one compressed rooted weighted G0
the same gate separately in both frozen FCC and HCP
a theorem converting C7's finite two-shell native slot-assignment space into one successor orbit

novelty_guard: Do not claim novelty merely because the update is local.
Do not claim novelty merely because explicit missing incidence data plus a base graph determines the augmented graph.
Do not claim novelty for quotienting augmentations by Aut(G,x) or for canonical isomorph-free enumeration.
Do not claim novelty merely from using an FCC neighborhood or a local topology-preservation criterion.

Any stronger theorem-facing claim must isolate a lattice-specific statement about recoverability/equivalence of native-realizable hidden completions from the compressed observable, or exhibit a harmful collision.
limitations: This is a documented high-recall web/primary-source audit, not an exhaustive MathSciNet/zbMATH/Scopus theorem-index search.
Some publisher pages exposed abstracts rather than full theorem bodies; such sources are used only for the precisely stated paper-level result visible there.
No absence result is global: 'no direct match' means no direct theorem was found in the audited source set and query families.
No literature similarity is treated as a proof of or against the C7 mathematical gate.
